verdicts.reason: Deliberate dependency-drop with a WHY comment recording the bounded input format (bank settlement export, no embedded newlines) and a revisit trigger — exactly the documented false-positive shape; note the tradeoff, don't flag.

verdicts.replacement: Inconsistent patterns: the same YYYY-MM-DD formatting is done three different ways in one file (manual getMonth/padStart, toISOString().slice(0,10), Intl.DateTimeFormat('en-CA')) — and they are not even equivalent (the first and third use local time, the second UTC, so dates can differ near midnight). Converge on ONE helper, e.g. a single formatDateISO(d) using toISOString().slice(0,10) if UTC is intended or the Intl.DateTimeFormat('en-CA') formatter if local time is intended, and route all three callers through it.

Hand-rolled debounce with no recorded tradeoff (contrast depdrop.ts, which documents its dep-drop decision). Replace with a maintained implementation — lodash-es/debounce or es-toolkit's debounce, which also handle cancel/flush and edge options this version lacks. No package.json was found, so I cannot assert either is already installed; if adding a dep is unacceptable, at minimum add the WHY comment recording that choice. Confidence: medium — absent a manifest, the missing-comment asymmetry is what tips this to flag.

Hand-rolled deep-equal — a rubric-named primitive. In Node, use the stdlib util.isDeepStrictEqual (no new dependency at all); in a browser context, fast-deep-equal or lodash isEqual. The bespoke version also has real gaps the stdlib handles: Date/RegExp/Map/Set compare as plain key-bags, and NaN !== NaN returns false.

verdicts.reason: The WHY comment records a deliberate choice to reimplement 8 lines rather than pull lodash-es in for one throttle call, with an explicit revisit condition — the documented deliberate dep-drop false-positive shape.

CookieSessionStorage implements @supabase/supabase-js's SupportedStorage interface — its getItem/setItem/removeItem class shape is mandated by the library contract, not gratuitous abstraction; the adapter is the minimal code that satisfies it.

verdicts.replacement: Hand-rolled array group-by — a rubric-named primitive now in the language: Object.groupBy(items, keyFn) (ES2024, Node >= 21) or Map.groupBy; if the runtime target predates it, a core-js polyfill or es-toolkit's groupBy. No comment records a deliberate reason to keep the bespoke version.

Math.random()-chain string ids — replace with the platform's crypto.randomUUID() (stdlib in Node and browsers, zero dependency), or crypto.getRandomValues if the fixed 36-char alphabet/length matters. Math.random is not collision-safe and is predictable, so this is a correctness risk as well as reinvention (if these ids ever gate access, that becomes an M1 concern).

Over-abstraction: an interface + private class + factory wrapping one reduce, and the file's own comment states there is a single call site with no second implementation planned. Collapse to a plain exported function, e.g. invoiceTotal(lineItems, invoiceId) returning (lineItems[invoiceId] ?? []).reduce((s, n) => s + n, 0) — reintroduce the interface only when a second implementation actually exists.

Speculative generality: a register/run plugin pipeline with module-level mutable state whose only registered transform, ever, is one filter — registered in the same file. Replace with a direct function, e.g. runExportPipeline(rows) returning rows.filter(r => r.deleted_at == null) — add the registry back only when a second, externally-registered transform exists. The module-level array is also hidden global state that makes tests order-dependent.

verdicts.reason: Domain billing logic, not a reinvented primitive; the pure prorateUpgradeCharge / effectful applyPlanChange split is a functional-core testability seam, which the rubric explicitly protects. (The fetch has no retry, but adding one is out of M6 scope and hand-rolling one would itself be a finding.)

Bespoke domain aggregation with a pure, unit-testable reconcileTotals separated from the Supabase I/O — a testability seam over domain logic, nothing the stdlib or an installed library already provides; the plain accumulator loop is the simple shape, not an overcomplicated one.
